title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_current_ratio() Measures short-term liquidity comparing current assets current liabilities. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range current ratio bounded zero unbounded . Values 1.0 mean current liabilities exceed current assets. empirical range nonprofits approximately 0,150, 15, organizations clustered 0.5 5. Benchmarks rules thumb 1.0: Conventional adequacy threshold – liabilities exactly covered. 0.5: Indicates acute short-term risk (Tuckman & Chang 1991). 3.0-4.0: May indicate excess cash slow receivables collection. Sector medians generally fall 1.0,2.51.0, 2.5 range (Zietlow et al. 2007). Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: cr = current_assets / current_liabilities  current_assets      = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable                       + investment_sales + prepaid_expenses current_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_quick_ratio() Measures liquidity using liquid assets, excluding inventory prepaid expenses. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range quick ratio bounded zero (asset values negative properly prepared balance sheet) unbounded . practice empirical range nonprofits approximately 0,100, 10, extreme values 5 typically indicating cash hoarding, unusually large receivables balance, organization minimal current liabilities (e.g., grant-making foundation accounts payable). Values zero can occur net receivables negative (allowances uncollectible pledges exceed gross pledges) denominator carries accounting adjustments. large values can result current liabilities near zero, producing ratios mathematically valid practically uninterpretable. default winsorization 1st/99th percentiles addresses extremes. Benchmarks rules thumb 1.0: Conventionally adequate; liquid assets cover current liabilities. 0.5-1.0: Potential short-term stress. 0.5: Common vulnerability threshold (Tuckman & Chang 1991). high values (3-5) may signal excess cash hoarding rather financial health. declining trend consecutive years stronger warning signal single year’s value. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: qr = quick_assets / current_liabilities  quick_assets        = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable current_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_cash_liquidity_ratio() Measures immediate liquidity using cash cash equivalents current liabilities. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero unbounded . ratio 1.0 means cash exactly covers current payables. empirical range nonprofits approximately 0,200, 20, values 0.1 5.0. high values common grant-making foundations endowed organizations carry minimal accounts payable. Benchmarks rules thumb 0.5: Organization cover half near-term payables cash alone; reliant receivables collection borrowing. 1.0 : Full cash coverage current liabilities. highly conservative measure, values somewhat 1.0 normal receivables healthy. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: casr = ( cash + savings ) / current_liabilities  current_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

what: Cash and Savings to Assets Ratio
title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_cash_assets_ratio() Cash savings share total assets; measures liquid composition asset base. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1: zero means liquid assets; one means entire asset base cash savings. practice nonprofits fall 0.05,0.500.05, 0.50 range. Values 0.60 uncommon operating nonprofits may indicate excess cash hoarding. Benchmarks rules thumb universally accepted benchmark. Values 0.05 suggest minimal liquid cushion; values 0.60 may indicate -deployment assets toward mission. Foundations endowed institutions naturally show higher ratios operating nonprofits. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: cash_assets = ( cash + savings ) / total_assets

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_cash_on_hand() Absolute dollar amount cash liquid savings held end year. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Cash hand bounded zero (negative properly prepared balance sheet) unbounded . Unlike ratio measures, scale dollars, comparison across organizations different sizes requires normalization. Use get_months_cash_operations() get_days_cash_operations() size-adjusted comparisons. Benchmarks rules thumb absolute measure, benchmarks depend organization’s expense base. common practitioner rule least 60-90 days operating expenses liquid cash. Nonprofit Finance Fund recommends minimum three months operating expenses accessible reserves. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: coh = cash + savings

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_cash_burn_ratio() Monthly rate organization draws cash reserves. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero (cash negative). Values 1.0 indicate cash depletion; values 1.0 indicate cash accumulation. Ratios near zero indicate near-complete cash exhaustion. ratio undefined (NA) beginning--year cash zero, occurs first year operation complete cash drawdown. Benchmarks rules thumb ratio consistently 1.0 multiple years warning sign; single year 1.0 may reflect planned reserve spending. 0.50 single year (cash halved) warrants investigation. ratio consistently 1.0 indicates accumulating liquidity reserves. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: brr = ( cash_boy - cash_eoy ) / months_in_period

what: Days of Operating Cash on Hand
title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_days_cash_operations() Measures many days organization can operate using available liquid assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero unbounded , expressed days. typical range nonprofits approximately 0,3650, 365. Values 365 (one year cash) indicate large liquid reserves relative expenses, uncommon operating nonprofits typical foundations. Benchmarks rules thumb 30 days: Generally considered distress indicator. 60-90 days: Commonly cited minimum threshold (Nonprofit Finance Fund). 90-180 days: Considered healthy operating nonprofits. Healthcare nonprofits typically benchmarked 150+ days due longer receivables cycles. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: doch = liquid_assets / daily_expenses  liquid_assets = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable daily_expenses = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 365

what: Days of Operating Cash and Investments
title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_days_cash_investments() Measures days operating coverage using liquid investment assets, net fixed property obligations. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Unbounded directions. Negative values occur unrestricted net assets negative (accumulated deficits exceed equity) fixed assets net debt exceed liquid resources. Values 365 indicate one year coverage. Benchmarks rules thumb 180-365 days: Considered solid reserve position endowed organizations. large gap metric get_days_cash_operations() indicates liquidity concentrated investments rather accessible cash. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: doci = investable_assets / daily_expenses  investable_assets = unrestricted_net_assets + investments                     - ( land_buildings_equipment + mortgages_payable ) daily_expenses    = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 365

what: Months of Operating Cash on Hand
title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_months_cash_operations() Number months organization can operate using available liquid assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero; unbounded . typical operating range nonprofits approximately 0,240, 24 months, values 12 months uncommon operating organizations (typical foundations). Benchmarks rules thumb Less 1 month: Acute liquidity risk. 1-3 months: adequate; common guidance least 3 months. 3-6 months: Generally considered healthy operating nonprofits. 6+ months: Strong reserve position. Nonprofit Finance Fund recommends 3-6 months target. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: moch = liquid_assets / monthly_expenses  liquid_assets    = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable monthly_expenses = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 12

what: Months of Liquid Unrestricted Net Assets (LUNA)
title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_liquid_assets_months() Number months organization can operate using liquid unrestricted net assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Unbounded directions, expressed months. Negative values indicate fixed property (net mortgage debt) exceeds unrestricted net assets. practical range operating nonprofits approximately −12,36-12, 36 months. Benchmarks rules thumb general benchmarks get_operating_reserve_ratio(): 3-6 months considered adequate operating nonprofits. Negative LUNA values particularly informative: indicate unrestricted equity entirely absorbed illiquid fixed assets. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: luna = liquid_unrestricted_net_assets / monthly_expenses  liquid_unrestricted_net_assets = unrestricted_net_assets                                  - ( net_fixed_assets - mortgages_payable ) monthly_expenses = total_expenses / 12

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_assets_ratio() Proportion total assets financed liabilities. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Theoretically bounded 0,10, 1 net assets positive: zero means debt; one means liabilities equal total assets (zero net assets). Values 1.0 occur total liabilities exceed total assets, .e., organization negative net assets (accumulated deficits exceed equity). distress indicator uncommon capital-intensive nonprofits (hospitals, housing) carrying large long-term debt. Benchmarks rules thumb 0.50: Generally considered financially stable. 0.50-0.70: Moderate leverage; manageable warrants monitoring. 0.70: High leverage; common vulnerability threshold (Tuckman & Chang 1991). 1.0: Negative net assets; acute financial risk. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: dar = total_liabilities / total_assets

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_equity_ratio() Compares total liabilities unrestricted net assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero liabilities non-negative unrestricted net assets positive. Unbounded unrestricted net assets small. Values zero occur unrestricted net assets negative (accumulated deficits exceed unrestricted equity), acute financial distress signal. ratio undefined (NA) unrestricted net assets equal zero. Benchmarks rules thumb Values 1.0 mean total liabilities less unrestricted equity base – generally considered strong. Values 1.0 3.0 indicate moderate leverage. Values 5.0 indicate high leverage relative equity base common vulnerability threshold. Negative values indicate negative unrestricted net assets, almost always signals significant financial stress. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: der = total_liabilities / unrestricted_net_assets

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_netassets_ratio() Compares total liabilities unrestricted net assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range get_debt_equity_ratio(): bounded zero numerator denominator positive; unbounded ; negative unrestricted net assets negative. Benchmarks rules thumb Values 3.0-5.0 commonly flagged high leverage nonprofit vulnerability literature. See get_debt_equity_ratio() fuller benchmark guidance. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: dmr = total_liabilities / unrestricted_net_assets

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_shortterm_ratio() Measures short-term obligations share total net assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero net assets positive. Negative values occur net assets negative (accumulated deficit), makes ratio uninterpretable burden measure. Unbounded net assets approach zero. Typical values financially stable nonprofits 0,0.300, 0.30 range. Benchmarks rules thumb Values 0.10 indicate modest short-term payables relative equity base – comfortable position. Values 0.30 suggest near-term obligations placing meaningful pressure net assets. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: stdr = short_term_liabilities / net_assets  short_term_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_secured_ratio() Secured mortgages notes payable share total liabilities. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1. nonprofits zero secured debt; capital-intensive organizations (housing, healthcare, higher education) can show values 0.70. Benchmarks rules thumb standard benchmark. informative tracked time compared within subsectors similar capital structures. organizations high secured debt ratios, lenders scrutinize collateral value debt service coverage ratio. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: debt_secured = secured_mortgages_notes / total_liabilities

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_debt_unsecured_ratio() Unsecured notes loans payable share total liabilities. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1. nonprofits carry unsecured notes, distribution highly concentrated zero long right tail. Benchmarks rules thumb established benchmark. Presence unsecured debt inherently negative – many healthy nonprofits use lines credit cash flow management – large growing ratio warrants scrutiny. Trend analysis informative single year’s value. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: debt_unsecured = unsecured_notes_loans / total_liabilities

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_equity_ratio() Share total assets financed net assets (equity). Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Theoretically bounded 0,10, 1 net assets positive. Values 1.0 possible. Values zero occur net assets negative (accumulated deficit), distress indicator. empirical range nonprofits approximately 0.10,0.950.10, 0.95. Benchmarks rules thumb 0.50: Equity finances half assets – generally healthy. 0.30: High leverage; common capital-intensive subsectors. useful trend measure: declining values warrant investigation. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: er = total_net_assets / total_assets

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_surplus_margin_ratio() Net surplus deficit share total revenue. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 1.0 (expenses negative). Bounded negative infinity theory, practice empirical range nonprofits approximately −0.30,0.30-0.30, 0.30 years. Values -0.50 0.50 typically reflect unusual one-time events (large gifts, major write-downs, asset sales). Benchmarks rules thumb Near zero: Normal expected nonprofits operating close break-even. 0.02-0.07 (2-7%): Commonly considered healthy surplus range. -0.05 two consecutive years: Common vulnerability threshold (Greenlee & Trussel 2000). Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: sm = revenues_less_expenses / total_revenue

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_return_assets_ratio() Net surplus deficit share total assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range ROA unbounded directions. ratio zero means expenses exactly equalled revenues. Positive values indicate surplus years; negative values indicate deficit years. nonprofits, perpetual surpluses raise concerns mission prioritization perpetual deficits signal sustainability risk, meaningful range approximately −0.20,0.20-0.20, 0.20 organizations years. Values outside range impossible typically reflect unusual circumstances (large asset disposals, one-time gifts, major capital campaigns, accounting restatements) rather stable operating performance. Values can distorted small total asset bases (newly formed organizations) organizations whose assets consist almost entirely illiquid fixed property, making denominator poor proxy operational resource base. Benchmarks rules thumb Near zero: Normal nonprofits operating close break-even design. 0.02-0.07 (2-7%): Generally considered healthy – building modest reserves without appearing hoard resources. Sustained -0.05: Common threshold classifying organization risk (Greenlee & Trussel 2000, Keating et al. 2005). Asset structure matters: capital-intensive organizations mechanically produce low ROA even financially healthy. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: roa = revenues_less_expenses / total_assets

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_return_netassets_ratio() Net surplus deficit share beginning--year net assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Unbounded directions. value 0 means break-even. typical range nonprofits approximately −0.30,0.30-0.30, 0.30. ratio undefined (NA) beginning net assets equal zero. Extreme values occur BOY net assets near zero (small denominator) rather surplus large. Benchmarks rules thumb Small positive values (0.02-0.10) considered healthy. Sustained negative RONA multiple years financial vulnerability indicator (Greenlee & Trussel 2000). useful trend analysis within-subsector comparisons. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: rona = revenues_less_expenses / net_assets_boy

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_profit_margin_postdepr() Operating surplus deficit share total revenue, depreciation. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 1.0; unbounded . typical range nonprofits approximately −0.30,0.30-0.30, 0.30. Extreme negative values may reflect major write-downs one-time capital expenses. Benchmarks rules thumb Near zero: Normal nonprofits operating close break-even. 0.02-0.07 (2-7%): Healthy. -0.05 two consecutive years: Common vulnerability threshold. persistent gap post- pre-depreciation margins signals capital consumption requiring future capital expenditure. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: podpm = ( total_revenue - total_expenses ) / total_revenue

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_profit_margin_predepr() Operating surplus deficit share total revenue, depreciation. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 1.0; unbounded . Always equal greater post-depreciation margin (get_profit_margin_postdepr()) since adding back depreciation can increase margin. typical range approximately −0.20,0.40-0.20, 0.40. Benchmarks rules thumb pre-depreciation margin zero post-depreciation margin zero common generally manageable capital-intensive nonprofits. margins negative, organization generating true cash flow deficit, just accounting loss. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: predpm = ( total_revenue - ( total_expenses - depreciation ) ) / total_revenue

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_self_sufficiency_ratio() Measures whether program service revenue sufficient cover total expenses. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero; values 1.0 possible (indicate program revenue exceeds total expenses - surplus earned income alone). typical range nonprofits approximately 0,1.50, 1.5, values 1.0 since nonprofits depend contributed income. Benchmarks rules thumb SSR > 1.0: Fully self-sufficient program revenue; characteristic mature social enterprises fee-based service providers. SSR 0.50-1.0: Majority costs covered program revenue; moderate philanthropy dependence. SSR < 0.25: Heavily dependent contributed income; common advocacy organizations, arts nonprofits, grant-funded research entities. High SSR universally better – organizations serving low-income populations often require philanthropic subsidy design. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.
code: ssr = program_service_revenue / total_expenses

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_program_expenses_ratio() Share total expenses devoted program services. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero one. Zero means spending programs (overhead); one means spending programs (administration fundraising). practice, values 0.95 unusual may reflect accounting misallocation. empirical range operating nonprofits approximately 0.50 0.95. Benchmarks rules thumb >= 75%: Charity Navigator threshold favorable efficiency score. >= 65%: BBB Wise Giving Alliance minimum standard. 50%: Commonly flagged concern, though legitimate startup-phase organizations. Caution: high ratios achieved underinvesting administration (“starvation cycle”) can signal long-term organizational weakness (Lecy & Searing 2015). Calculated : 990 filers .
code: per = program_expenses / total_expenses

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_overhead_ratio() Combined management fundraising expenses share total expenses. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1. Empirical range approximately 0.05,0.500.05, 0.50 operating nonprofits. Benchmarks rules thumb 25% less: Charity Navigator threshold full efficiency score. 35% less: BBB Wise Giving Alliance standard. Low overhead can indicate underinvestment organizational capacity (“starvation cycle”) rather genuine efficiency. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: overhead = ( mgmt_expenses + fundraising_expenses ) / total_expenses

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_expenses_admin_ratio() Share total expenses devoted management general administration. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1. combination program fundraising ratios, three sum 1.0 construction. empirical range nonprofits approximately 0.05,0.350.05, 0.35. Benchmarks rules thumb Charity Navigator targets management general expenses 15% total expenses favorable score. Values 5% may indicate underinvestment governance systems. Calculated : 990 filers .
code: aer = management_expenses / total_expenses

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_fundraising_efficiency_ratio() Cost raising one dollar contributions; measures efficiently fundraising expenses generate donated revenue. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded zero; values 1.0 (spending dollar raise dollar) possible, particularly young organizations building donor bases difficult fundraising environments. typical range approximately 0,0.500, 0.50 operating nonprofits. Benchmarks rules thumb <= 10 cents per dollar (ratio <= 0.10): Charity Navigator threshold full fundraising efficiency score. <= 35 cents per dollar: BBB Wise Giving Alliance standard. 50 cents: Commonly flagged inefficient. Calculated : 990 filers .

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_expenses_compensation_ratio() Total compensation employee-related expenses share total functional expenses. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1. service-delivery nonprofits fall 0.50,0.850.50, 0.85 range. Grant-making organizations may show ratios 0.20. Benchmarks rules thumb universal benchmark – labor intensity varies fundamentally mission type. Human services, health, education nonprofits typically show ratios 0.60; grant-making organizations may show ratios 0.30. sharp year--year increase may indicate revenue contraction rather compensation growth. Calculated : 990 filers .

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_expenses_grants_ratio() Total grants paid domestic organizations, domestic individuals, foreign entities share total functional expenses. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1. Near zero direct-service organizations; near 1.0 pure pass-grant-makers. Benchmarks rules thumb Subsector comparisons essential: 0.80 ratio expected community foundation; value anomalous hospital. Rising ratios time may indicate strategic shift toward redistributive model. Calculated : 990 filers .

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_grants_govt_ratio() Share total revenue originating government grants. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1. Zero means government funding; one means revenue comes government sources. empirical distribution varies widely subsector: social service organizations often show ratios 0.50; arts organizations typically 0.20. Benchmarks rules thumb Values 0.50 indicate majority government-funded organizations, face heightened vulnerability government budget changes. Revenue diversification theory suggests maintaining single source 0.33-0.50 optimal stability (Chang & Tuckman 1994). Calculated : 990 filers .

title: Fiscal metrics catalog

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_netassets_composition_ratio() Share total net assets unrestricted available general use. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Bounded 0,10, 1 numerator denominator positive: zero means net assets restricted; one means net assets unrestricted. Values outside range occur either unrestricted total net assets negative. Benchmarks rules thumb 0.50: least half net assets unrestricted – generally healthy. 0.20: Heavy donor-restricted balance sheet; limited flexibility. Organizations large permanent endowments may show low ratios without financial weakness. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.

title: Fiscal metrics catalog
text: get_netassets_growth_ratio() Year--year change total net assets, expressed proportion beginning net assets. Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Unbounded directions. value 0 means net assets unchanged. Values -1.0 (drop 100%) indicate organization lost entire starting equity base, resulting negative net assets. ratio undefined (NA) BOY net assets equal zero. Benchmarks rules thumb Small positive values (0.01-0.10) typical healthy operating nonprofits. -0.10 single year warning sign; sustained negative growth indicates structural financial problem. high positive values (0.50) often reflect one-time large gifts asset revaluations rather sustained operational performance. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.

title: Fiscal metrics catalog

Formula: Input variables Definitional Range Unbounded directions expressed months. Negative values occur unrestricted net assets negative net fixed assets exceed unrestricted net assets. Values 24 months uncommon operating organizations may indicate accumulation beyond needed operating risk management. Benchmarks rules thumb Less 1 month: Acute vulnerability. 1-3 months: commonly recommended minimum. 3-6 months: Generally adequate operating nonprofits. 6-12 months: Strong; appropriate volatile-revenue capital-intensive organizations. Nonprofit Finance Fund recommends minimum 3 months. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.

title: Normalization & transformations
text: Winsorization transformation need know variable’s theoretical support — program-expense ratio lives [0, 1]; growth rate can negative; dollar amount non-negative unbounded . range argument encodes : support determines winsorization clips transformation appropriate. winsorize_x() exposes winsorization step directly:
code: w <- winsorize_x(ratio, range = "zp", winsorize = 0.98)  c(bottom = w$bottom, top = w$top) #>    bottom       top  #> -0.001000  3.755658 sum(w$is_sentinel)     # observations pushed to a bound #> [1] 11

title: Normalization & transformations
text: Standardizing badly skewed variable produces badly skewed z-score. multivariate work — correlations, factor analysis, fiscal-health index — want indicator approximately normal first. find_best_normalization() choosing, per variable, one four transformations based shape stable interior (non-sentinel, non-missing values left winsorization). procedure always : Winsorize set aside sentinel (boundary) observations pile-bounds can’t distort fit. Diagnose stable interior — support, boundary mass, zero inflation. Select transformation diagnostics (accept explicit vtype). Fit transformation’s parameters robust center/scale (median / MAD). Report --skewness kurtosis can see whether transformation actually helped. Separating fit apply means fitted model can score later panel year identical scale — see apply_normalization() end.

title: Normalization & transformations
text: guess_normalize_type() implements decision rule. Writing p0 share values zero, p1 share one, using boundary_mass_cutoff 0.10: four transformations, distribution pathology one targets:
code: is the variable effectively in [0, 1]?  (range "zo", or >98% of values in [0,1]) ├── yes │    ├── p0 > 0.10  ........................  hurdle       (zero-inflated) │    ├── p1 > 0.10  ........................  rank_normal  (piled up at the top) │    └── otherwise  ........................  logit        (well-spread proportion) └── no      ├── non-negative? (range "zp", or min >= 0)  ....  asinh   (heavy right tail)      └── mixed / irregular support  ................  rank_normal

title: Normalization & transformations
text: Pathology. Non-negative amounts long right tail: handful huge organizations stretch scale (dollar figures, days cash). Transform. inverse hyperbolic sine asinh(x / s), scaled s, median absolute non-zero value stable interior. behaves like identity near zero like log tails, defined zero, accommodates negatives.  raw skewness 2 collapses toward zero, extreme kurtosis tamed.
code: set.seed(1) x_asinh <- rlnorm(2000, meanlog = 10, sdlog = 1.3)   # e.g. total-asset dollars  fit <- find_best_normalization(x_asinh, range = "zp", verbose = FALSE) c(type = fit$transform_type,   raw_skew = round(fit$raw_skewness, 2), fit_skew = round(fit$fit_skewness, 2),   raw_kurt = round(fit$raw_kurtosis, 2), fit_kurt = round(fit$fit_kurtosis, 2)) #>     type raw_skew fit_skew raw_kurt fit_kurt  #>  "asinh"   "2.56"   "0.81"   "7.44"  "-0.19"  plot_normalize_x(x_asinh, range = "zp")

title: Normalization & transformations
text: Pathology. ratio bounded [0, 1] mass spread middle little pile-ends (many expense- revenue-share ratios). Transform. Rescale [0, 1] relative theoretical support, apply qlogis() (log-odds), stretches bounded scale onto whole real line.
code: set.seed(2) x_logit <- rbeta(2000, 2, 8)   # a right-skewed share ratio  fit <- find_best_normalization(x_logit, range = "zo", verbose = FALSE) c(type = fit$transform_type,   raw_skew = round(fit$raw_skewness, 2), fit_skew = round(fit$fit_skewness, 2)) #>     type raw_skew fit_skew  #>  "logit"   "0.81"  "-0.53"  plot_normalize_x(x_logit, range = "zo")

title: Normalization & transformations
text: Pathology. [0, 1] variable spike exact zeros — organizations simply don’t thing (fundraising, grants, debt) — mixed continuous positive part. Treating zeros ordinary small numbers wrong; qualitatively different. Transform. Zeros retained 0; positive part transformed separately (rank logit) rescaled positive interval. trigger p0 > boundary_mass_cutoff.  zero spike preserved group positive component spread .
code: set.seed(4) x_hurdle <- c(rep(0, 900), rbeta(1100, 2, 5))   # ~45% structural zeros  fit <- find_best_normalization(x_hurdle, range = "zo", verbose = FALSE) c(type = fit$transform_type, p0_reason = fit$guess_reason) #>                                                                     type  #>                                                                 "hurdle"  #>                                                                p0_reason  #> "Variable is effectively in [0,1] with substantial zero mass (p0=0.45)."  plot_normalize_x(x_hurdle, range = "zo")

title: Normalization & transformations
text: Pathology. Anything parametric transforms can’t handle gracefully: bimodal distributions, mixed positive/negative support clean model, [0, 1] variable piled top. Transform. rank-based inverse normal transform maps empirical ranks onto Gaussian. preserves ordering distances, robust almost shape — cost discarding original spacing.  bimodal shape (strongly negative kurtosis) pulled toward single normal mode.
code: set.seed(3) x_rank <- c(rnorm(1000, -3), rnorm(1000, 4))   # bimodal, mixed support  fit <- find_best_normalization(x_rank, range = "np", verbose = FALSE) c(type = fit$transform_type,   raw_kurt = round(fit$raw_kurtosis, 2), fit_kurt = round(fit$fit_kurtosis, 2)) #>          type      raw_kurt      fit_kurt  #> "rank_normal"       "-1.75"       "-0.02"  plot_normalize_x(x_rank, range = "np")

title: Normalization & transformations
text: normalize_x() runs fit--apply single call — handy one-variable: need transformation applied new data (different panel year, holdout sample), fit re-apply, scored identical scale: Force specific transformation vtype want override auto-detection:
code: z <- normalize_x(x_asinh, range = "zp", verbose = FALSE) round(c(mean = mean(z), sd = sd(z)), 3) #>  mean    sd  #> 0.315 1.062 fit  <- find_best_normalization(x_asinh, range = "zp", verbose = FALSE) z_new <- apply_normalization(rlnorm(50, 10, 1.3), fit = fit) normalize_x(x, range = "np", vtype = "rank_normal")

title: Panel smoothing
text: panel_smooth(): preserves panel dimensions column names, handles beginning end series without dropping observations, supports equal, half, decay weighting, re-normalizes weights around missing values. particularly useful stabilizing noisy longitudinal financial measures keeping time point interpretable.

title: Building a 990 panel
text: get_panel() downloads multiple years IRS 990 e-file data stacks one long-format panel, stamping row TAX_YEAR (optionally) attaching Business Master File metadata. rest article use small hand-built panel mimics messiness real e-file data — amended returns, group returns, gap:
code: # a four-year panel with the default financial tables panel <- get_panel(years = 2019:2022)  dim(panel) table(panel$TAX_YEAR)  # skip the BMF join (faster; attach later with merge_bmf()) panel <- get_panel(years = 2019:2022, include_bmf = FALSE) mk <- function(ein, yr, grp = "", amd = "", stamp, rev) {   data.frame(     EIN2 = ein, TAX_YEAR = yr,     RETURN_GROUP_X = grp, RETURN_PARTIAL_X = "", RETURN_AMENDED_X = amd,     RETURN_TIME_STAMP = stamp,     F9_08_REV_TOT_TOT = rev, F9_09_EXP_TOT_TOT = round(rev * 0.9),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) }  panel <- do.call(rbind, list(   mk("A", 2019, stamp = "2020-05-01", rev = 500000),   mk("A", 2020, stamp = "2021-05-01", rev = 520000),   mk("A", 2021, stamp = "2022-05-01", rev = 560000),   mk("B", 2019, stamp = "2020-05-01", rev = 300000),   mk("B", 2019, amd = "X", stamp = "2020-09-01", rev = 310000),  # amended duplicate   mk("B", 2021, stamp = "2022-05-01", rev = 340000),             # 2020 missing   mk("C", 2020, grp = "X", stamp = "2021-05-01", rev = 800000),  # group return   mk("C", 2020, stamp = "2021-05-20", rev = 810000),   mk("C", 2021, stamp = "2022-05-01", rev = 790000) ))  knitr::kable(panel[, c("EIN2", "TAX_YEAR", "RETURN_GROUP_X",                        "RETURN_AMENDED_X", "F9_08_REV_TOT_TOT")])

title: Building a 990 panel
text: E-file data can contain several filings organization-year: amended returns, partial-year returns, group returns. inspect_duplicates() diagnoses problem without changing data: deduplicate() reduces panel one record per EIN2 × TAX_YEAR using ordered rules — drop group returns, drop partial-year returns, keep recent filing RETURN_TIME_STAMP. rule drop every record organization-year, rows rescued passed next rule.
code: dups <- inspect_duplicates(panel)  dups$summary_types #>   filing_type rows_total rows_kept rows_dropped #> 1      normal          2         1            1 #> 2     amended          1         1            0 #> 3       group          1         0            1 panel_dd <- deduplicate(panel, verbose = FALSE)  nrow(panel)      # before #> [1] 9 nrow(panel_dd)   # after #> [1] 7

title: Building a 990 panel
text: actually observed, ? panel_composition() classifies organization’s presence across panel window. Ask per-ID classification table return_classification = TRUE: organization labelled persistent, entrant, exit, transient, empty, panel_spell seamless segmented (segmented spell gap year). attach columns data instead, use append_classification = TRUE; panel_summary() reports overall shape panel: Keep organizations want analyze panel_filter_types() — example, organizations observed throughout window: panel_impute() can fill short internal gaps selected panel types smoothing scoring:
code: cls <- panel_composition(panel_dd, return_classification = TRUE, print_table = FALSE)  cls[, c("EIN2", "panel_type", "panel_year_count", "panel_gap_count")] #>   EIN2 panel_type panel_year_count panel_gap_count #> 1    A persistent                3               0 #> 4    B persistent                2               1 #> 6    C    entrant                2               0 panel_cls <- panel_composition(panel_dd, append_classification = TRUE, print_table = FALSE)  panel_summary(panel_cls, print_table = FALSE) persistent <- panel_filter_types(panel_dd, panel_types = cls, keep = "persistent")  unique(persistent$EIN2) #> [1] "A" "B" panel_imp <- panel_impute(   panel_dd,   panel_types = cls,   types       = "persistent",   vars        = "F9_08_REV_TOT_TOT" )

title: Building a 990 panel
text: panel_smooth() replaces selected numeric fields rolling within-organization average, leaving panel’s shape unchanged. real panel pass field scope ("PZ", "PC", ""); name columns directly: panel_smooth() article covering window logic equal / half / decay weighting schemes: see vignette("panel-smoothing").
code: panel_sm <- panel_smooth(   panel_dd,   vars   = c("F9_08_REV_TOT_TOT", "F9_09_EXP_TOT_TOT"),   window = 3 )

title: Building a 990 panel
text: compute_all_panel() panel-aware sibling compute_all(): computes full battery fiscal-health metrics within TAX_YEAR, winsorization, standardization, percentile ranks year-relative. result clean, smoothed, scored panel — one row per organization-year, ready longitudinal analysis composite index (vignette("fiscal-health-index")).
code: panel_scored <- compute_all_panel(panel_sm, metrics = c("ratio", "z"), verbose = FALSE)  new_cols <- setdiff(names(panel_scored), names(panel_sm)) length(new_cols) #> [1] 2 head(new_cols) #> [1] "profit_postdepr"   "profit_postdepr_z"

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: fiscal turns IRS 990 financial data standard set nonprofit fiscal-health metrics — liquidity, leverage, margins, efficiency, reserves — computed way every time results comparable across organizations years. Every get_*() metric function appends four columns data (raw, winsorized, z-score, percentile rank), compute_all() runs entire battery . pairs panel990, retrieves normalizes underlying 990 e-file panels: assemble clean data panel990, score fiscal.

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: ~50 fiscal-health ratios — curated library liquidity, leverage, profitability, efficiency, reserve metrics documented formulas. Four versions per metric — raw, winsorized (_w), standardized (_z), percentile rank (_p), outliers scale never distort comparisons. One-call scoring — compute_all() appends every metric data frame. Sensible 990 defaults, overridable — function defaults correct e-file field names accepts column names. Pipe-enabled form-aware — handles full 990 990-EZ filers; blank financials interpreted correctly via sanitize_financials(). Panel-ready — retrieve, deduplicate, smooth multi-year panels thin wrappers panel990, score every organization-year.

Usage Arguments df: data.frame containing required fields computing metric. metric appended dataset. debt: Column name(s) total liabilities. (990: Part X, line 26B; F9_10_LIAB_TOT_EOY. EZ: Part II, line 26B; F9_01_NAFB_LIAB_TOT_EOY.) assets: Column name(s) total assets, EOY. (990: Part X, line 16B; F9_10_ASSET_TOT_EOY. EZ: Part II, line 25B; F9_01_NAFB_ASSET_TOT_EOY.) winsorize: winsorization value (0 1), defaults 0.98 winsorizes 1st 99th percentile values. sanitize: TRUE (default), imputes zero NA values financial fields computing ratio, respecting form scope. summarize: TRUE, prints summary statistics plots density curves four output columns. metrics argument controls versions returned: append_to_df argument controls output shape:

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: package includes three functions building preparing multi-year panel datasets IRS 990 efile data.

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Downloads multiple years IRS 990 efile data stacks single long-format panel. year retrieved independently via retrieve_efile_data(), stamped TAX_YEAR, combined dplyr::bind_rows() — columns appear years others filled NA.
code: # Retrieve a 4-year panel with default tables (P00, P01, P08, P09, P10) panel <- get_panel( years = 2019:2022 )  dim( panel ) table( panel$TAX_YEAR )  # Retrieve without BMF metadata (faster; attach manually later) panel <- get_panel( years = 2019:2022, include_bmf = FALSE )

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: IRS 990 efile data can contain multiple filings per organization per year (amended returns, partial-year returns, group returns). deduplicate() reduces panel one record per EIN2 × TAX_YEAR using three ordered heuristics: Drop group returns — RETURN_GROUP_X == "X" Drop partial-year returns — RETURN_PARTIAL_X == "X" Keep recent — retain filing latest RETURN_TIME_STAMP applying drop rule eliminate records organization-year, records rescued passed next step. function prints report showing records dropped step, year, frequency table many filings existed per organization-year deduplication.
code: panel_clean <- deduplicate( panel )  # Suppress the report panel_clean <- deduplicate( panel, verbose = FALSE )

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Applies centered rolling window average within organization’s time series reduce year--year noise financial variables. Returns data frame identical dimensions column names — selected numeric columns replaced smoothed values. vars argument selects columns smooth: Three weighting schemes available:
code: # Full panel workflow panel       <- get_panel( years = 2019:2022 ) panel_clean <- deduplicate( panel )  # Smooth PZ-scope financial fields with a 3-year window panel_smooth_pz <- panel_smooth( panel_clean, vars = "PZ", window = 3 )  # Smooth specific columns with decay weighting and a 5-year window panel_smooth_custom <- panel_smooth(   panel_clean,   vars    = c( "F9_01_REV_TOT_CY", "F9_01_EXP_TOT_CY", "F9_10_ASSET_TOT_EOY" ),   window  = 5,   weights = "decay" )  # Compute all fiscal health ratios on the cleaned, smoothed panel panel_ratios <- compute_all( panel_smooth_pz )

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: following accounting ratios included package:

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Asset Revenue Ratio Definition: Measures revenue generated per dollar assets. Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: assets_rev = total_assets_eoy / total_revenue

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Cash Savings Assets Ratio Definition: Cash savings share total assets; measures liquid composition asset base. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: cash_assets = ( cash + savings ) / total_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Burn Rate Ratio Definition: Rate organization depletes cash reserves relative prior period. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: cash_burn = cash_eoy / cash_boy

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Cash Liquidity Ratio Definition: Measures organization’s ability cover current liabilities using cash savings. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: cash_liq = ( cash + savings ) / ( accounts_payable + grants_payable )

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Cash Hand Definition: Absolute dollar amount liquid cash holdings (cash plus savings). Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: cash_on_hand = cash + savings

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Current Ratio Definition: Measures short-term liquidity comparing current assets current liabilities. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: current = current_assets / current_liabilities  current_assets      = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable                       + investment_sales + prepaid_expenses current_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Days Cash Investments Definition: Days operating coverage including investment assets net related debt. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: days_cash_inv = liquid_and_investment_assets / daily_expenses  liquid_and_investment_assets = unrestricted_net_assets + investments                                - ( land_buildings - mortgages_payable ) daily_expenses               = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 365

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Days Cash Hand Definition: Number days organization can operate using available liquid assets. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: days_cash_ops = liquid_assets / daily_expenses  liquid_assets  = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable daily_expenses = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 365

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Debt Asset Ratio Definition: Proportion total assets financed liabilities. Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: debt_assets = total_liabilities / total_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Debt Equity Ratio Definition: Compares total liabilities unrestricted net assets. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: debt_equity = total_liabilities / unrestricted_net_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Debt Net Assets Ratio Definition: Compares total liabilities unrestricted net assets. Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: debt_netassets = total_liabilities / unrestricted_net_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Secured Debt Ratio Definition: Secured mortgages notes payable share total liabilities. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: debt_secured = secured_mortgages_notes / total_liabilities

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Short Term Debt Ratio Definition: Share short-term liabilities relative total net assets. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: debt_shortterm = short_term_liabilities / net_assets  short_term_liabilities = accounts_payable + grants_payable

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Unsecured Debt Ratio Definition: Unsecured notes loans payable share total liabilities. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: debt_unsecured = unsecured_notes_loans / total_liabilities

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Donation Grant Dependence Ratio Definition: Measures reliance contributions fundraising share total revenue. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: donations_rev = ( contributions + fundraising_revenue ) / total_revenue

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Earned Income Dependency Ratio Definition: Share total revenue earned program commercial income sources. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: earned_income = earned_revenue / total_revenue  earned_revenue = program_service_rev + membership_dues + royalties + other_revenue

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Equity Ratio Definition: Share total assets financed net assets (organizational equity). Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: equity = net_assets / total_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Administrative Overhead Ratio Definition: Share total expenses devoted management general administration. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_admin = administrative_expenses / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Payments Affiliates Ratio Definition: Payments affiliates share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_affiliates = payments_to_affiliates / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Compensation Expense Ratio Definition: Total compensation employee-related expenses share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_compensation = ( officer_comp + disqualified_comp + other_salaries                           + pension_contributions + other_employee_benefits                           + payroll_taxes ) / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Fees Services Ratio Definition: Total fees paid outside professional services share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_feesforservice = ( mgmt_fees + legal_fees + accounting_fees + lobbying_fees                             + prof_fundraising_fees + investment_mgmt_fees                             + other_fees ) / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Grants--Others Expense Ratio Definition: Total grants paid domestic foreign entities share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: expenses_grants = ( us_org_grants + us_indiv_grants + foreign_grants )                   / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Member Benefits Expense Ratio Definition: Benefits paid members share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: expenses_membbenefits = member_benefits / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Fundraising Efficiency Ratio Definition: Cost raising one dollar contributions; lower values indicate efficient fundraising. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: fundr_eff = fundraising_expenses / total_contributions

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Government Grant Ratio Definition: Share total revenue originating government grants. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: grants_govt = government_grants / total_revenue

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Investment Income Dependency Ratio Definition: Measures reliance investment-related revenue share total revenue. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: invest_income = investment_income / total_revenue  investment_income = invest_income + bond_proceeds + rent_income + asset_sale_income

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Investment Assets Ratio Definition: Investment securities share total assets. Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: investments_assets = ( pub_traded_securities + other_securities ) / total_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Land, Buildings, Equipment Assets Ratio (Gross) Definition: Gross book value land, buildings, equipment share total assets, netting accumulated depreciation. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: land_assets_gross = land_bldg_equip_deprec / total_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Land, Buildings, Equipment Assets Ratio (Net) Definition: Net land, buildings, equipment share total assets, accumulated depreciation. Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: land_assets_net = land_bldg_equip_net / total_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Liquid Unrestricted Net Assets (Months) Definition: Unrestricted net assets available operations, net illiquid fixed assets related debt, expressed months expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: liquid_assets_months = ( unrestricted_net_assets - net_fixed_assets + mortgages_payable )                        / monthly_expenses  monthly_expenses = total_expenses / 12

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Months Cash Hand Definition: Number months organization can operate using available liquid assets. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: months_cash_ops = liquid_assets / monthly_expenses  liquid_assets    = cash + savings + pledges_receivable + accounts_receivable monthly_expenses = ( total_expenses - depreciation ) / 12

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Net Assets Composition Ratio Definition: Share total net assets unrestricted available general operations. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: netassets_comp = unrestricted_net_assets / total_net_assets

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Net Assets Growth Ratio Definition: Year--year change net assets proportion beginning--year net assets. Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: netassets_growth = ( net_assets_eoy - net_assets_boy ) / net_assets_boy

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Operating Reserve Ratio Definition: Months operating expenses covered liquid unrestricted net assets. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: op_reserve = ( unrestricted_net_assets - net_fixed_assets ) / monthly_expenses  monthly_expenses = total_expenses / 12

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Overhead Ratio Definition: Combined management fundraising expenses share total functional expenses. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: overhead = ( mgmt_expenses + fundraising_expenses ) / total_expenses

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Post-Depreciation Profit Margin Definition: Operating surplus deficit share total revenue, depreciation. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: profit_postdepr = ( total_revenue - total_expenses ) / total_revenue

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Pre-Depreciation Profit Margin Definition: Operating surplus deficit share total revenue, depreciation. Formula: Scope: 990 filers
code: profit_predepr = ( total_revenue - ( total_expenses - depreciation ) ) / total_revenue

title: fiscal • Nonprofit Fiscal Health Metrics
text: Ratio: Program Expense Ratio Definition: Share total expenses devoted program services. Formula: Scope: 990 + 990EZ filers
code: prog_exp = program_expenses / total_expenses

what: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
title: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
text: apply_transformations() central post-computation step called every get_*() ratio function. produces four versions ratio: raw (_raw): unmodified computed ratio. winsorized (_w): outliers clipped bounds determined range argument winsorize proportion, via winsorize_x(). normalized (_z): distribution-appropriate transformation winsorized values. Parameters fitted stable interior (non-NA, non-sentinel observations) via find_best_normalization(), scored full vector via apply_normalization(), sentinel pile-winsorization bounds distort centering spread estimates. percentile (_p): integer percentile rank (1-100) based raw values, via dplyr::ntile().

title: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
code: apply_transformations(   x,   winsorize = 0.98,   offset = 0.001,   range = "np",   normalize_type = NULL )

title: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
text: x Numeric vector (computed ratio, transformation). winsorize Winsorization proportion 0 1 (default 0.98, clips 1st 99th percentiles "np" range). offset Sentinel offset applied fixed bounds (default 0.001). Observations clipped fixed bound stored bound -- offset remain identifiable _w column. range Character string describing theoretical range ratio. Controls lower upper winsorization bounds determined: "np" Negative positive (unbounded directions). Winsorizes symmetrically (1-winsorize)/2 1-(1-winsorize)/2 percentiles. Default behaviour. "zp" Zero positive. lower bound fixed -offset (flagging truncated--zero values) upper bound winsorize percentile full distribution. "zo" Zero one. bounds fixed (-offset 1+offset), flagging values outside [0, 1]. percentile-based clipping applied. "nz" Negative zero. upper bound fixed +offset lower bound 1-winsorize percentile. "lo;hi" Custom numeric range, e.g. "0;10". lower bound fixed lo - offset upper bound hi + offset. normalize_type Transformation type override passed find_best_normalization(). One NULL (auto-detect), "asinh", "logit", "rank_normal", "hurdle". Default NULL.

title: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
text: named list elements raw, winsorized, z, pctile.

title: Apply winsorization, normalization, and percentile ranking to a ratio vector — apply_transformations
text: Winsorization Delegated entirely winsorize_x(), handles range codes, computes sentinel flags, returns winsorized vector alongside diagnostic metadata. Normalization (_z column) find_best_normalization() called first fit transformation parameters (type, scale constant, center, spread) stable interior winsorized distribution. apply_normalization() scores full original vector using fitted parameters. two-step design means fitted model can reused new data needed. Percentile rank (_p column) Integer percentile rank 1 100 based raw (pre-winsorized) values, computed dplyr::ntile().

what: Compute all fiscal health metrics year-by-year across a panel — compute_all_panel
title: Compute all fiscal health metrics year-by-year across a panel — compute_all_panel
text: panel-safe wrapper around compute_all() splits data year, computes every fiscal health metric independently within year's slice, stacks results. ensures winsorization bounds, normalization parameters, percentile ranks estimated cross-sectional distribution single year rather pooled multi-year distribution. year--year computation matters: compute_all() passes raw ratio vector apply_transformations(), fits winsorization bounds normalization model data receives. pooled panel distributions mixture N years, : ratio 95th percentile 2021 may rank 80th percentile pooled distribution 2022—2024 values higher. Winsorization clips pooled extremes, year-specific extremes. Z-scores centred scaled pooled moments. Splitting year computing avoids three problems: every _w, _z, _p column interpretable within-year percentile standardised value, exactly single-year call compute_all().

TRUE (default), returns original df metric columns appended. text: Internally function: Validates year present panel contains one year (single-year panel works warning issued since compute_all() give identical results). Tags row original position output rows can restored input order splitting stacking. Splits df list single-year slices using data.table::split(). Calls compute_all() slice verbose passed per-year messages visible (suppressed) requested. Stacks per-year results data.table::rbindlist(), handles columns present years absent others (e.g. 990EZ-year lacks Part VIII columns) filling NA. Restores original row order drops internal row-tag column.

text: large panels (e.g. 5 years – 50 000 orgs) per-year loop runs compute_all() five times ~50 000-row slices rather 250 000-row frame. slice call faster uses less peak memory; data.table::rbindlist() stack O(N) copies.

title: Debt to Asset Ratio — get_debt_assets_ratio
text: Proportion total assets financed liabilities. Formula:   Definitional Range Theoretically bounded [0, 1] net assets positive: zero means debt; one means liabilities equal total assets (zero net assets). Values 1.0 occur total liabilities exceed total assets, .e., organization negative net assets (accumulated deficits exceed equity). distress indicator uncommon capital-intensive nonprofits (hospitals, housing) carrying large long-term debt. Benchmarks rules thumb 0.50: Generally considered financially stable. 0.50-0.70: Moderate leverage; manageable warrants monitoring. 0.70: High leverage; common vulnerability threshold (Tuckman & Chang 1991). 1.0: Negative net assets; acute financial risk. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.

title: Operating Ratio — get_netassets_growth_ratio
text: net assets growth ratio measures year--year percentage change total net assets - essentially organizational equivalent return equity growth. Positive values indicate organization grew equity base year (surplus plus balance sheet adjustments); negative values indicate net asset erosion (deficit write-downs). ratio captures changes net assets, including unrealized investment gains, prior-period adjustments, currency translation effects, just operating surplus. therefore broader measure get_return_netassets_ratio(), uses revenues-less-expenses figure.

title: Operating Reserves Ratio — get_operating_reserve_ratio
text: Liquid unrestricted net assets available cover operating expenses, expressed multiple total annual expenses. Formula:   Definitional Range Unbounded directions expressed months. Negative values occur unrestricted net assets negative net fixed assets exceed unrestricted net assets. Nonprofit Finance Fund recommends minimum 3 months. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.

title: Operating Reserves Ratio — get_operating_reserve_ratio
text: operating reserve ratio answers key sustainability question: many months operations can organization fund unrestricted liquid assets, excluding illiquid fixed property? recommended primary reserve adequacy metric Nonprofit Finance Fund widely used financial health assessments, lender due diligence, board reporting. Unlike days/months cash measures (get_days_cash_operations(), get_months_cash_operations()), count cash receivables, operating reserve ratio starts full unrestricted equity base removes fixed assets - giving broader picture liquid reserves available sustain operations.

title: Post-Depreciation Profitability Margin — get_profit_margin_postdepr
text: Operating surplus deficit share total revenue, depreciation. Formula:   Definitional Range Bounded 1.0; unbounded . typical range nonprofits approximately [-0.30, 0.30]. Extreme negative values may reflect major write-downs one-time capital expenses. Benchmarks rules thumb Near zero: Normal nonprofits operating close break-even. 0.02-0.07 (2-7%): Healthy. -0.05 two consecutive years: Common vulnerability threshold. persistent gap post- pre-depreciation margins signals capital consumption requiring future capital expenditure. Calculated : 990 filers .

title: Pre-Depreciation Profitability Margin — get_profit_margin_predepr
text: pre-depreciation profit margin approximates cash flow operations adding back non-cash depreciation charges surplus. Since depreciation accounting allocation past capital expenditure rather current cash outflow, measure better reflects organization's actual cash-generating ability. positive pre-depreciation margin alongside negative post-depreciation margin indicates organization cash-flow positive "booking" loss due large depreciation charges.

title: Pre-Depreciation Profitability Margin — get_profit_margin_predepr
text: (Total revenue - (Total expenses - Depreciation)) / Total revenue. Equivalently, (revenue - expenses + depreciation) / revenue. simplest cash flow approximation available 990 data; account changes working capital, capital expenditures, debt service, directly reported 990. EBITDA margin used commercial analysis similar spirit also adds back interest, taxes, amortization. pre-depreciation margin adds depreciation (amortization included), making conservative approximation.

title: Program Expense Ratio — get_program_expenses_ratio
text: Share total expenses devoted program services. Formula:   Definitional Range Bounded zero one. Zero means spending programs (overhead); one means spending programs (administration fundraising). practice, values 0.95 unusual may reflect accounting misallocation. empirical range operating nonprofits approximately 0.50 0.95. Benchmarks rules thumb >= 75%: Charity Navigator threshold favorable efficiency score. >= 65%: BBB Wise Giving Alliance minimum standard. 50%: Commonly flagged concern, though legitimate startup-phase organizations. Caution: high ratios achieved underinvesting administration ("starvation cycle") can signal long-term organizational weakness (Lecy & Searing 2015). Calculated : 990 filers .

title: Quick Ratio — get_quick_ratio
text: Measures liquidity using liquid assets, excluding inventory prepaid expenses. Formula:   Definitional Range quick ratio bounded zero (asset values negative properly prepared balance sheet) unbounded . practice empirical range nonprofits approximately [0, 10], extreme values 5 typically indicating cash hoarding, unusually large receivables balance, organization minimal current liabilities (e.g., grant-making foundation accounts payable). Values zero can occur net receivables negative (allowances uncollectible pledges exceed gross pledges) denominator carries accounting adjustments. large values can result current liabilities near zero, producing ratios mathematically valid practically uninterpretable. default winsorization 1st/99th percentiles addresses extremes. Benchmarks rules thumb 1.0: Conventionally adequate; liquid assets cover current liabilities. 0.5-1.0: Potential short-term stress. 0.5: Common vulnerability threshold (Tuckman & Chang 1991). high values (3-5) may signal excess cash hoarding rather financial health. declining trend consecutive years stronger warning signal single year's value. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.

title: Quick Ratio — get_quick_ratio
text: quick ratio (also called acid-test ratio) short-term liquidity measure asks whether organization pay current obligations immediately, using assets can converted cash within days weeks rather months. Unlike current ratio (get_current_ratio()), excludes inventory prepaid expenses, less reliably liquid. nonprofits distinction especially meaningful: prepaid expenses (insurance premiums, deposits) recovered quickly, including liquidity test misleading. quick ratio useful detecting near-term insolvency risk, stress-testing organization's ability absorb sudden revenue disruption, comparing liquidity positions across organizations different sizes. common component multi-ratio financial health scoring models nonprofit literature.

title: Quick Ratio — get_quick_ratio
text: standard -profit formula (Brigham & Houston 2019) defines quick assets cash + marketable securities + net receivables, current liabilities obligations due within one year. Nonprofit applications require two adaptations: Receivables: Pledges receivable included nonprofit version normal operating asset defined cash-timeline. analysts exclude multi-year pledges (current-year portion truly liquid), 990 Part X break pledges current vs. long-term portions, full net amount used . Current liabilities: -profit firms sum current liabilities (accounts payable, short-term debt, accrued liabilities, current portion long-term debt, deferred revenue, etc.). 990 balance sheet label liabilities current vs. long-term. implementation uses accounts payable plus grants payable best available proxy near-term obligations, following Tuckman & Chang (1991) Greenlee & Trussel (2000). Mortgage notes payable (line 23B) excluded long-term nature, unsecured notes (line 24B) excluded typically carry defined maturity dates outside 12-month window. alternative numerator used analysts (Hager 2001) adds short-term investments held sale (F9_10_ASSET_INV_SALE_EOY) grounds can liquidated quickly. field excluded many nonprofits classify long-term endowment holdings line, making unreliable current asset proxy.

title: Return on Assets — get_return_assets_ratio
text: Net surplus deficit share total assets. Formula:   Definitional Range ROA unbounded directions. ratio zero means expenses exactly equalled revenues. Positive values indicate surplus years; negative values indicate deficit years. nonprofits, perpetual surpluses raise concerns mission prioritization perpetual deficits signal sustainability risk, meaningful range approximately [-0.20, 0.20] organizations years. Values outside range impossible typically reflect unusual circumstances (large asset disposals, one-time gifts, major capital campaigns, accounting restatements) rather stable operating performance. Values can distorted small total asset bases (newly formed organizations) organizations whose assets consist almost entirely illiquid fixed property, making denominator poor proxy operational resource base. Benchmarks rules thumb Near zero: Normal nonprofits operating close break-even design. 0.02-0.07 (2-7%): Generally considered healthy – building modest reserves without appearing hoard resources. Sustained -0.05: Common threshold classifying organization risk (Greenlee & Trussel 2000, Keating et al. 2005). Asset structure matters: capital-intensive organizations mechanically produce low ROA even financially healthy. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.

title: Self Sufficiency Ratio — get_self_sufficiency_ratio
text: Measures whether program service revenue sufficient cover total expenses. Formula:   Definitional Range Bounded zero; values 1.0 possible (indicate program revenue exceeds total expenses - surplus earned income alone). typical range nonprofits approximately [0, 1.5], values 1.0 since nonprofits depend contributed income. Benchmarks rules thumb SSR > 1.0: Fully self-sufficient program revenue; characteristic mature social enterprises fee-based service providers. SSR 0.50-1.0: Majority costs covered program revenue; moderate philanthropy dependence. SSR < 0.25: Heavily dependent contributed income; common advocacy organizations, arts nonprofits, grant-funded research entities. High SSR universally better – organizations serving low-income populations often require philanthropic subsidy design. Calculated : 990 + 990EZ filers.

what: Normalize a numeric vector for multivariate analysis — normalize_x
title: Normalize a numeric vector for multivariate analysis — normalize_x
text: Convenience wrapper calls find_best_normalization() apply_normalization() single step. repeated application fitted model use functions directly. function winsorizes x according range winsorize, isolates stable interior (non-sentinel, non-NA values) fit transformation parameters, scores observations – including sentinels – using fitted parameters. prevents boundary pile-winsorization bounds distorting centering spread estimates. Four transformation types supported: "asinh": inverse hyperbolic sine, scaled median absolute nonzero value stable interior. Defined zero, accommodates negatives, behaves like log tails. "logit": maps stable interior [0, 1] relative theoretical support, applies qlogis(). Suited variables bounded [0, 1] without heavy boundary mass. "rank_normal": rank-based inverse normal transform. Preserves ordering, distances. Robust irregular shapes mixed support. "hurdle": structural-zero mass receives 0; positive values transformed separately (rank logit) rescaled positive interval. vtype = NULL type auto-detected stable interior using heuristics based support range boundary mass.

text: x Numeric vector (computed ratio, transformation). winsorize Winsorization proportion 0 1 (default 0.98, clips 1st 99th percentiles "np" range). offset Sentinel offset applied fixed bounds (default 0.001). Observations clipped fixed bound stored bound -- offset remain identifiable _w column. range Character string describing theoretical range ratio. Controls lower upper winsorization bounds determined: "np" Negative positive (unbounded directions). Winsorizes symmetrically (1-winsorize)/2 1-(1-winsorize)/2 percentiles. Default behaviour. "zp" Zero positive. lower bound fixed -offset (flagging truncated--zero values) upper bound winsorize percentile full distribution. "zo" Zero one. bounds fixed (-offset 1+offset), flagging values outside [0, 1]. percentile-based clipping applied. "nz" Negative zero. upper bound fixed +offset lower bound 1-winsorize percentile. "lo;hi" Custom numeric range, e.g. "0;10". lower bound fixed lo - offset upper bound hi + offset. normalize_type Transformation type override passed find_best_normalization(). One NULL (auto-detect), "asinh", "logit", "rank_normal", "hurdle". Default NULL.
